title: Opposition leaders and students detained in Chandigarh over CEC protests
seoTitle: Chandigarh protests over CEC and voter rolls

tea.why: Protesters and opposition leaders demonstrated against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged voter-list manipulation.
tea.want: Demanding the resignation of the Chief Election Commissioner and an end to voter suppression.
tea.changed: Oct 12: Panjab University students clashed with police at Sector 17 Plaza during a march against the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls.

summary: Opposition leaders and student organizations held demonstrations in Chandigarh and Delhi against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The protests were sparked by allegations of voter-list manipulation and the removal of millions of voters from electoral rolls during the Special Intensive Revision exercise. In Chandigarh, the ruling Aam Aadmi Party held a demonstration near the state election commission office, resulting in the detention of leaders such as Manish Sisodia and Harpal Singh Cheema by police. Separately, students from Panjab University marched toward the Punjab Election Commission office demanding the CEC's resignation. The student march led to confrontations and clashes with police at Sector 17 Plaza, resulting in brief detentions and allegations of police misconduct. Protesters accused the central government of curbing democratic rights and manipulating electoral processes.
demands: Resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar
Halt to voter-list manipulation and the SIR exercise
response: According to the sources, police used barricades and detained several opposition leaders and students during the demonstrations. Protesters alleged that police manhandled students and that male officers tore female protesters' clothes without female personnel present.

arrests.text: Two students were detained during the protest and later released

updates.text: Opposition leaders from CPI-M and AAP faced detention in Delhi and Chandigarh during protests against CEC Gyanesh Kumar.
Panjab University students clashed with police during a march against the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls.
